questions.question: Which language and text direction should the portfolio use?
questions.rationale: The brief is in Hebrew and a right-to-left interface best fits the intended audience.

options.label: Hebrew + English
options.description: A bilingual interface with language switching.

questions.question: Which code language should be used for the React/Vite frontend?
questions.rationale: The existing scaffold is a React/Vite TypeScript project.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Type-safe React components for the existing TypeScript scaffold.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should be used?
questions.rationale: The repository already uses React with Vite.

questions.question: Provide your display name, short professional bio, role/title, profile photo, and contact links (email, LinkedIn, GitHub, or other relevant links).
questions.recommendedChoice: Use concise, professional placeholder-style copy until final details are supplied
questions.rationale: Personal identity and contact details are essential to an effective self-presentation portfolio.
questions.answer: Use concise, professional placeholder-style copy until final details are supplied

questions.question: How many projects should be presented, and what details should each include (title, summary, image, technologies, live URL, source code, and outcomes)?
questions.recommendedChoice: 4 projects with title, summary, technologies, image, and live/source links
questions.rationale: A compact initial portfolio gives a complete project showcase without overloading the first version.
questions.answer: 4 projects with title, summary, technologies, image, and live/source links

questions.question: Which visual direction should the portfolio use?
questions.rationale: A restrained, responsive visual style keeps projects prominent and is suitable for a broad technical audience.

options.label: Modern minimal
options.description: Clean typography, generous spacing, subtle motion, and strong project imagery.

options.label: Bold expressive
options.description: Larger type, vivid color accents, and an energetic editorial layout.

options.label: Elegant professional
options.description: Refined neutral colors and a polished, formal presentation.

questions.question: Confirm the essential portfolio sections and interactions. Use a free-text response to add or remove anything.
questions.recommendedChoice: Hero/about, project gallery with filters, skills, contact links, responsive navigation, and subtle motion
questions.rationale: These sections cover self-introduction, project discovery, qualifications, and conversion to contact.
questions.answer: Hero/about, project gallery with filters, skills, contact links, responsive navigation, and subtle motion

sharedQuestions.question: Does this portfolio need data persistence, uploads, queues, caching, or file/object storage?
sharedQuestions.rationale: Project content can ship as static typed data in the frontend, so no backend persistence is required.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Keep project and profile content in static frontend files.

sharedQuestions.question: Will visitors need to sign in to use application API features?
sharedQuestions.rationale: The requested portfolio is a public presentation site with no private API features.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Visitors must authenticate for protected features.

sharedQuestions.question: Should the finished static portfolio be deployed to Azure Static Web Apps?
sharedQuestions.rationale: Azure Static Web Apps is a natural fit for a React/Vite portfolio and supports a simple deployment workflow.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Provision Azure Static Web Apps and prepare deployment configuration.

options.label: No
options.description: Keep the project local and production-ready, but do not provision Azure hosting.

notes: Initial React/Vite scaffold exists. No code implementation should begin until requirements are confirmed and the project plan is approved.
